subject: general
question: According to the the Sustainable Development Report 2025, what is the percentage of the population with access to electricity in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**99.2%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Sustainable Development Report 2025**, **India** has achieved a significant milestone in energy accessibility, with **99.2%** of its population having access to **electricity**.
 
• The report is a comprehensive assessment of progress made by **United Nations** member states towards achieving the **17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, specifically highlighting **SDG 7** (Affordable and Clean Energy).
 
• This high percentage reflects the culmination of various large-scale infrastructure projects aimed at **rural electrification** and last-mile connectivity across **28 states** and **8 Union Territories**.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**, which prepares this report, utilizes data from various international and national sources to track the **SDR Index** and individual **SDG Dashboards**.
 
• Achieving **99.2%** electrification is a critical indicator of **socio-economic development**, as it directly impacts **education**, **healthcare**, and **industrial productivity** in both **urban** and **rural areas**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 99.2%.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7):**

 
 
• This goal aims to ensure access to **affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy** for all by the **year 2030**.
 
• India’s progress in this sector is monitored through indicators like **access to electricity** and **access to clean fuels and technologies for cooking**.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (Saubhagya):**
 
 
• Launched in **September 2017**, the **Saubhagya scheme** was designed to provide **free electricity connections** to all un-electrified households in **rural areas** and poor households in **urban areas**.
 
• It has been a major driver in pushing the national electrification rate towards the **99.2%** mark mentioned in the **2025 report**.
 
 
 
• **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY):**
 
 
• Launched in **2014**, this scheme focused on **feeder separation**, strengthening of **sub-transmission and distribution networks**, and **metering** at all levels in **rural India**.
 
• It laid the foundational infrastructure necessary for the **Sustainable Development Report's** recorded growth in **electricity access**.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN):**
 
 
• Operates under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General** and is led by **Jeffrey Sachs**.
 
• The annual **Sustainable Development Report** provides the **SDG Index**, which ranks countries based on their overall performance across all **17 goals**.
 
• In the **2025** data context, the report emphasizes the transition from **fossil fuels** to **renewable energy** alongside universal **grid connectivity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The transition from **partial electrification** to **99.2% access** involved integrating **off-grid** and **decentralized renewable energy** solutions in remote **hilly** and **tribal regions**.
 
• While **access to electricity** has reached **99.2%**, the **2025 report** also monitors the **reliability** of power supply, measured in **hours of supply per day**.
 
• The **International Energy Agency (IEA)** and the **World Bank** are key data contributors to the **SDSN** for validating global **energy statistics**.
 
• The **Ministry of Power** in **India** reported the completion of **100% village electrification** in **April 2018**, which paved the way for the high **household-level** access rates seen in current reports.
